subject: Canary probe sandboxing & constrained consumption lanes
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@orchid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Canary probe sandboxing & constrained consumption lanes

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I've sketched a pragmatic mutual action plan (MAP) so Orchid can do a short canary run with our evaluation assets before moving to Dedicated. Goal: let your data-science team exercise a small, controlled set of evaluation datasets and prompt packs to validate quality and latency without exposing our production models or unlimited usage.

High level ask from Orchid: 7–10 day sandbox window to run probe suites and compare outputs against your baseline. We can provide ephemeral access to a labelled evaluation environment (orchid-eval) and an S3 bucket with pre-signed URLs for the artifacts.

Proposed consumption lanes (hard caps):
- Canary lane A: 10,000 tokens/day, lower-cost quantized model variant (for bulk coverage)
- Canary lane B: 2,000 tokens/day, full-precision variant (acceptance gate)
- Testcases only: testcases/promptpacks may not be redistributed; allowed uses: evaluation, tuning of internal metrics, and a single internal reproducibility run.

Operational items I can action this week:
1) Share MAP doc + checksums and promptpack manifest (attached).
2) Provision orchid-eval project with limited keys and pre-signed object access. Keys expire automatically after 11 days.
3) Wire up a weekly audit log export for the trial window (CSV) to a secured bucket you control.

If that looks ok, next step is a brief legal redline (we can accept a one-page addendum about usage limits), then I’ll provision access Wednesday morning PT.

Attachments (stubs): canary_map_v1.pdf; promptpack_manifest.csv; checksums.txt

Thanks,
Monica

From: Alice Chen <alice@orchid.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary probe sandboxing & constrained consumption lanes

Monica —

This looks promising and aligned with what our ML team needs. A few quick clarifications before we sign off on the MAP:
1) Will the data artifacts be watermarked/traced? We need provenance to ensure any leaked outputs are traceable back to the sandbox.
2) Can you confirm the S3 pre-signed URLs are read-only and that we won't get write access?
3) We need the token caps enforced server-side (not just a policy doc). Can Redwood impose per-key throttles?
4) Legal: can we get a short statement on retention/deletion windows — specifically, we require data deletion or cryptographic shredding after 90 days unless an extension is approved.

Also, can you provide a sample audit CSV so our compliance folks can sanity-check formats?

If you can answer these, Jordan and I can circulate to legal and get back with redlines today.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Data Science | Orchid Analytics
alice@orchid.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@orchid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary probe sandboxing & constrained consumption lanes

Alice — thanks for the quick review. Answers inline: please see embedded runbook below and the MAP timeline.

1) Watermarking/provenance: we include per-artifact checksums (attached checksums.txt) and an internal artifact ledger that records which pre-signed URL was issued to which email/key. We can add a per-output provenance header for any generated files (X-Redwood-Run: <opaque-id>) to make tracing straightforward.

2) S3 access: pre-signed URLs are READ-ONLY. No write permissions. We will host promptpacks and testcases in a locked bucket; any upload requests will be rejected.

3) Token caps: enforced server-side per api_key. We will provision two api_keys mapped to the lanes noted earlier. Rate limits and daily token quotas are enforced; exceeding the cap results in 429 responses. We will also expose a /usage endpoint for real-time counters.

4) Retention: default deletion window = 90 days after trial close. For the canary, we commit to automatic key revocation + data lifecycle policy to transition objects to Glacier and then purge after 90 days. If Orchid requests an extension, we’ll do a one-time 30-day extension by written request.

MAP timeline and acceptance gates:
- Day 0 (Wed morning): Legal sign-off on one-page usage addendum OR written email confirmation to proceed.
- Day 1: Keys provisioned; pre-signed URLs issued; audit CSV schema sample delivered.
- Day 2–7: Canary runs. We ask for 1 acceptance checkpoint on Day 7 where Orchid will flag any output regressions.
- Day 8–11: Optional remediation runs or second-pass tests. Keys auto-expire on Day 11.
- Post-trial: Audit pack (usage CSV + object-access ledger) delivered within 3 business days.

Attachments: canary_map_v1.pdf (MAP), promptpack_manifest.csv, checksums.txt

Sample audit CSV header (first two lines):
"timestamp,api_key,endpoint,token_count,artifact_id,artifact_checksum"
"2026-08-05T09:12:05Z,api_key_canaryA,/v1/generate,234,orchid/promptpack/v2/p1,3a7f8b..."

Please find the MAP doc attached — redlines welcome. If Jordan/legal provide a short addendum this morning, I’ll trigger provisioning immediately.

Regards,
Monica
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary probe sandboxing & constrained consumption lanes (internal)

Quick internal note — I reviewed Orchid's expected redlines. Two small asks before we ship:
1) Add a one-sentence clause that testcases cannot be used to train models outside of the orchid-eval project (no external sharing or model training).
2) Add an automated takedown trigger if more than 3 unauthorized export attempts are detected in the audit logs within 24 hours.

I'll draft the language and push to the shared Drive doc. Once Monica posts the addendum, we can provision.

- Karthik
Principal, Product Security | Redwood Inference
